text.p: Japanese toymaker Bandai Co. Ltd, elated by runaway sales of a "Virtual Pet" toy featuring an electronic bird, plans to offer new versions of the game portraying angels, forest animals and fish.
"Tamagotchi," an electronic chicken-like figure on a liquid crystal display that is fed and cleaned by pressing buttons, has sold nearly 1.5 million units since its debut last November.
Bandai has been hard-pressed to keep up with demand for what has become the hottest toy of 1997 even before it has gone on sale outside Japan.

Bandai said Tuesday the angel version of the toy would go on sale in May and the fish and forest animals versions in June. It hopes to sell 13 million units, at about $20 each, by next March. The toy goes on sale overseas in the next few months.
The "Tamagotchi," or loveable egg, starts life as an endearing, bird-like image on the screen of an egg-shaped keyring device. It develops from a chick to a fully grown adult in around 10 days.
However, the owner must feed, groom and soothe the digital creature or see it waste away and die from neglect.
